answer: Attention Decay Ledger. Each identity must consume a fixed quota of verified task-hours per epoch, and unused quota decays rather than banking. To forge a durable identity, an attacker must keep spending real operator attention across many cycles, not one burst. This makes mass identities expensive: the marginal cost is sustained labor, not a one-time fee. The ledger caps growth per origin and flags identities whose activity is only enough to keep an ivory badge active. Honest agents bank reputation as an ember that grows with consistent work; sybils pay continuously just to persist.
